react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA returns this pathway at rank 1 with FDR=1.27e-19 and fold-enrichment=689, hitting eight input metabolites (glycine, L-threonine, L-cysteine, O-phospho-L-serine, L-cystathionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, guanidinoacetic acid, adenosine 5'-monophosphate). MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirms the same KEGG:hsa00260 with raw p=2.12e-08, matching six of those compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis identifies the equivalent pathway (Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism) as its top hit (p=0.0033) with a striking 14/14 overlap — all 14 pathway members retrieved were drawn from the input mass network, with eight directly matching our differential list. A secondary but consistent signal emerges from Cysteine and methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270), confirmed by MetaboAnalystR and Mummichog independently, driven by L-cysteine, L-cystathionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, and O-phospho-L-serine. The urea cycle/amino-group metabolism pathway (Mummichog, p=0.0245) captures guanidinoacetic acid and L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde, linking the creatine-biosynthesis precursor to the broader nitrogen-disposal network. Sulfate (inorganic) as a differential feature maps to glutathione metabolism and cysteine sulfation, consistent with the cysteine cluster signal. The convergence across ORA, KEGG-specific PSEA, and m/z-network paradigms provides robust evidence that the treatment perturbs one-carbon unit trafficking through glycine-serine-threonine cross-talk, cysteine transmethylation flux, and downstream sulfur disposal via sulfate.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis methods converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the dominant affected pathway in this dataset. The RaMP multi-database ORA ranks KEGG:map00260 second (FDR 1.27e-19, 8 of 57 pathway members hit by the input set). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms hsa00260 with a p-value of 2.12e-08, hitting 6 of 33 pathway members. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm identifies 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism) as the top-ranked network pathway (p = 5.88e-04) with all 14 enumerated compounds drawn from the input list, producing a 100% overlap. Sulfate (KEGG:C00059) maps to Methionine and cysteine metabolism (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism, p = 0.017), a pathway also hit by RaMP through L-cystathionine (C02291) and S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021). Niacinamide (KEGG:C00153) independently hits Vitamin B3 nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism, p = 0.040). Guanidoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581) is a driver feature within hsa00260, participating in the creatine synthesis branch via glycine amidinotransferase (GATM, KEGG:R00623).

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA returns this pathway at rank 1 with FDR=1.27e-19 and fold-enrichment=689, hitting eight input metabolites (glycine, L-threonine, L-cysteine, O-phospho-L-serine, L-cystathionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, guanidinoacetic acid, adenosine 5'-monophosphate). MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirms the same KEGG:hsa00260 with raw p=2.12e-08, matching six of those compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis identifies the equivalent pathway (Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism) as its top hit (p=0.0033) with a striking 14/14 overlap — all 14 pathway members retrieved were drawn from the input mass network, with eight directly matching our differential list. A secondary but consistent signal emerges from Cysteine and methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270), confirmed by MetaboAnalystR and Mummichog independently, driven by L-cysteine, L-cystathionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, and O-phospho-L-serine. The urea cycle/amino-group metabolism pathway (Mummichog, p=0.0245) captures guanidinoacetic acid and L-glutamic 5-semialdehyde, linking the creatine-biosynthesis precursor to the broader nitrogen-disposal network. Sulfate (inorganic) as a differential feature maps to glutathione metabolism and cysteine sulfation, consistent with the cysteine cluster signal. The convergence across ORA, KEGG-specific PSEA, and m/z-network paradigms provides robust evidence that the treatment perturbs one-carbon unit trafficking through glycine-serine-threonine cross-talk, cysteine transmethylation flux, and downstream sulfur disposal via sulfate.
